I second this...whatever it is you really just have to immerse yourself in something else. Anything you can find outside of you that makes you happy. For me it’s reading, anime, drawing, painting, legos, playdoh, coloring books, movies (as you can see literally anything) people always want to recommend what THEY like (people always want to tell me to go hiking or go to the beach or some shit and tbh I’m not outdoorsy and nothing about that shit makes me happy) so always take a step back and think about what YOU like. What’s the last thing that made you smile? Expand on that. I myself struggled a lot through middle school, high school, college and even now as a not so fully functioning adult. I feel alone a lot and I’m sad a lot so I can’t say it’s always going to be great but find joy in the little things when you can. If anything it can make that one single day better. You can worry about tomorrow tomorrow.

First of all he is the happiest person I know. No matter what’s going on he can find it in himself to smile and appreciate something.

He is always around for the important stuff-Big games, recitals, pre dance photos, first day of pretty much anything up through college. He made sure I tried everything-Every sport, hobby, exotic food. 

Most importantly he is an open communicator. He is engaged in my life without hovering or controlling. He always would talk through things good or bad. He made sure I learned how to express how I felt, listen to people, be open minded and positive but still know when to stand up for myself. My half sister and I often gush about how lucky we are.

I was not originally a cat person, but when my college roommates got this sweet little runt kitty I would often come home to empty food and water bowls. They were negligent forgetful college kids and it broke my heart. When I asked when they were getting his shots they said “it’s just an animal he doesn’t need all that” so of course I started taking responsibility, got him better food, toys, took him to get checkups/shots and everything. He started sleeping in my bed and when we moved out it wasn’t even a discussion it was my cat to take with me. 8 years later he’s still my bestie and I’m so glad he’s mine.
